meta.title: Deep-link scrolling in a legacy React Native app

highlight.caption: Deep links to any section of a screen

blocks.text: New deep links had to land users on specific sections inside complex legacy screens. Unlike the web, React Native has no “scroll to this element by id”.

An invisible **anchor** component that marks a target area (no style, no layout, just a reference), plus a **hook** that scrolls the parent ScrollView to it. Using it meant wrapping the target and calling one function.
Timing. When a deep link opened a screen, the target was often not where it would end up:

items: a collapsible around it could be closed;
a tab switch could be pending;

blocks.text: The solution only scrolls once the target is rendered and measured, and it adds an offset for headers that appear while scrolling.

items.label: Component
items.text: Accepts every way it can be placed.

items.label: Hook
items.text: Its logic and the calls it makes.

blocks.text: Visual checks and QA covered the rest.
Adopted across several screens, including tab switches and a collapsible. I also validated it inside a SectionList, so future list cases wouldn’t need a rewrite.
Making it generic was the team’s suggestion; I implemented it and solved the hard parts.

Screens with deep prop drilling forced an extra anchor to reach the parent ScrollView. I’d look for a more native way to resolve that reference instead of wrapping a View, and check existing libraries before building.
